name: DBMS & SQL
blurb: Short videos only: every pick is 20 minutes or less and covers one or two ideas, ordered so each subtopic is a sequence you can finish in sittings. Subtopics follow CS631 (Silberschatz 7e, chapters 10 and 12–23) after the SQL and design basics.
method:
• Length: hard cap of 20 minutes per video. Depth comes from a sequence of short lectures rather than one long one.
  • Order: picks in a subtopic are in watching order; the first is the starting point.
  • Sources: university courses published in short parts: Berkeley CS186, Jens Dittrich (Saarland), TU Kaiserslautern, Stanford's Jennifer Widom and Martin Kleppmann (Cambridge), plus single-concept explainers where those courses have gaps (Thomas' write rule, validation, snapshot isolation).
  • Coverage: chapters follow the CS631 syllabus; topics stressed in the 2024 and 2025 endsems (partitioning, validation, semijoins, RAID, bitmaps, ARIES, 2PC) each have their own video.

subtopics.name: Short-video courses
subtopics.note: Every video on this page is 20 minutes or less and covers one or two ideas, so a chapter is a sequence of short sittings. These series are where most of them come from; each is worth following end to end.
